§ 2Content

§ 3DIVERSITY IN LIVING ORGANISMS

  • Diversity refers to the variety of living organisms on Earth. It is the range of differences in form, structure, behaviour, and habitat among living things.
  • Classification (taxonomy) is the scientific process of arranging organisms into groups based on shared characteristics, making the study of diversity manageable.

Taxonomy

  • Taxonomy is the science of describing, naming, and classifying organisms, including all plants, animals, and microorganisms.
  • Carolus Linnaeus is the Father of Taxonomy. He published "Systema Naturae" in 1735 and proposed the Two Kingdom Classification in 1758.

Types of Classification Systems

#### 1. Two Kingdom Classification (1758)

  • Proposed by Carolus Linnaeus (1758).
  • Kingdoms: Plantae (all plants, algae, fungi) + Animalia (all animals).

#### 2. Three Kingdom Classification (1866)

  • Proposed by Ernst Haeckel (1866). He coined the term Ecology.
  • Kingdoms: Plantae + Animalia + Protista (new — for unicellular organisms: Amoeba, Paramecium, Euglena).

#### 3. Five Kingdom Classification (1969)

  • Proposed by R.H. Whittaker (1969).
  • Basis of classification: cell structure, mode of nutrition, body organization, reproduction.
  • Kingdoms:
  • Monera — prokaryotes (bacteria, blue-green algae).
  • Protista — eukaryotic unicellular.
  • Fungi — eukaryotic, multicellular (some unicellular), heterotrophic, spore-producing.
  • Plantae — autotrophic, multicellular.
  • Animalia — heterotrophic, multicellular.

#### 4. Three Domain Classification (1990)

  • Proposed by Carl Woese (1990).
  • Domains:
  • Bacteria — true prokaryotes (e.g. E. coli).
  • Archaea — microorganisms in extreme environments (e.g. Halobacterium); distinct from bacteria.
  • Eukarya — all eukaryotic organisms (Protists, Fungi, Plants, Animals).

Types of Classification Axes

  • Cell nature: Prokaryotes / Eukaryotes.
  • Cell occurrence: Unicellular / Multicellular.
  • Mode of nutrition: Autotrophs / Heterotrophs.
  • Level of body organization: Cellular / Tissue / Organ / Organ System.
